name: NEW ZEALAND
tagline: Land of the Long White Cloud

flag.title: Blue Ensign+Stars
flag.note: Union Jack + 4 red stars of Southern Cross

lead: New Zealand is two islands at the bottom of the world. The Māori named it Aotearoa, the Land of the Long White Cloud. It has fiery volcanoes and ancient reptiles. Many Lord of the Rings scenes were filmed here.
geo: New Zealand sits on the Ring of Fire, with active volcanoes and bubbling mud pools. Snowy Southern Alps and deep fjords like Milford Sound fill the South Island.
The North Island has steaming geysers. Most Kiwis live here. Auckland, the biggest city, sits between two harbours. Wellington, the capital, is at the southern tip.
animals: New Zealand split from Gondwana 80 million years ago, before mammals arrived. So birds took every job. The kiwi sniffs out worms with nostrils at its beak tip.
The tuatara looks like a lizard, but it is the last of a reptile family from the age of dinosaurs. The kākāpō is the world's heaviest parrot.
culture: The haka is a Māori dance of stamping and chanting. The All Blacks rugby team performs it before every match. In a hongi greeting, people press noses together.
A hāngi is a feast cooked underground on hot stones. Pavlova is meringue piled with cream and kiwifruit. New Zealand and Australia both say they invented it.
history: The Māori sailed here from Polynesia around 1300 CE, guided by stars and ocean swells. Dutch explorer Abel Tasman spotted the islands in 1642.
In 1840, the Crown and more than 500 Māori chiefs signed the Treaty of Waitangi. New Zealand became self-governing in 1907.
wows: In 1893, New Zealand became the first country to let women vote.
Scientists confirmed in 2017 that a sunken continent lies under New Zealand.
Seven penguin species swim in New Zealand waters, more than anywhere else.
Henry the tuatara became a dad at age 111.
New Zealand has about 4.6 sheep per person.
The world's first commercial bungee jump opened at Queenstown in 1988.
All three Lord of the Rings films were shot at over 150 places.

myths.myth: New Zealand is part of Australia
myths.fact: It is a separate country, 2,000 km across the Tasman Sea, with its own government.
Most people speak English. About 4 in 100 can chat in Māori.
